findings.message: `.skip-link:focus` has `display: none`, which means the skip link is permanently invisible even when keyboard-focused. The comment '/* in contact-pane this isn't there */' suggests this was added incorrectly. This completely defeats the purpose of a skip link and breaks keyboard navigation accessibility. It should be `display: block` or similar to reveal the element on focus.
findings.tp_fp_justification: Verified in the file: `.skip-link` has `display: none` in its base rule, and `.skip-link:focus` also sets `display: none`. A skip link that stays hidden on focus is non-functional — keyboard users can never reveal it. The comment suggests the author was unsure whether to include `display: none` here, not that it was intentional.
findings.severity_justification: Skip links are an accessibility feature for keyboard users. Having the skip link permanently hidden on focus defeats its purpose and breaks keyboard navigation, but it is a dev/local-only CSS file rather than production code.
findings.category_justification: This is a failure in a skip link implementation, which is a keyboard navigation accessibility feature.

findings.message: `import 'solid-ui/components/footer'` appears twice (lines 1 and 5). The `declare module 'solid-ui/components/footer'` on line 4 lacks a body block `{}`, making it an empty ambient declaration that is likely unintentional. TypeScript may emit a duplicate-import error or silently de-duplicate the side-effect import, but this is clearly a copy-paste mistake that should be cleaned up.
findings.tp_fp_justification: Verified in the file: `import 'solid-ui/components/footer'` appears on both line 1 and line 5, and line 4 has `declare module 'solid-ui/components/footer'` without a body block `{}`. This is a clear copy-paste artifact — the duplicate import is redundant and the empty module declaration without a body is not valid ambient module syntax.
findings.severity_justification: TypeScript/bundlers typically de-duplicate side-effect imports so there's likely no runtime impact. The empty `declare module` without a body is odd but won't cause a build failure. It is purely a code quality/maintainability concern.
findings.category_justification: Duplicate imports and a malformed ambient declaration are code quality issues that should be cleaned up.

findings.message: `showDashboard` cache reuse check compares `existingDashboard.dataset.subject` against the subject URI, but `globalAppTabs` only sets `div.dataset.globalPaneName` — it never sets `dataset.subject`. This means the equality check always fails, the `dashboardContainer.innerHTML = ''` branch always runs, and a new dashboard is always constructed from scratch on every `showDashboard` call. The optimization is completely ineffective.
findings.tp_fp_justification: Verified: `globalAppTabs` sets only `div.dataset.globalPaneName` (line 342) and never sets `dataset.subject`. The cache reuse check in `showDashboard` (lines 538-539) requires both `existingDashboard.dataset.globalPaneName === options.pane` AND `existingDashboard.dataset.subject === (subject.value || '')`. Since `dataset.subject` is always `undefined`, the equality check always fails and the dashboard is always reconstructed from scratch, making the cache optimization completely ineffective.
findings.severity_justification: The cache bypass means the dashboard is fully re-rendered on every `showDashboard` call, causing unnecessary work and potential visual flicker. However it doesn't cause incorrect behavior — just inefficiency and wasted UI operations.
findings.category_justification: The optimization logic is incorrect — the condition checking `dataset.subject` will never be true because that attribute is never set, defeating the intended caching behavior.

findings.message: `navMenuContent.addEventListener('click', ...)` is placed outside the `if (!navMenuContent.dataset.authEventsBound)` guard. The auth event listeners above are de-duplicated by the `authEventsBound` flag, but the click listener is not. If `createLeftSideMenu` is called more than once (e.g., `initMainPage` called again), a second click handler is registered: every menu item click would fire `setActiveMenuItem` and `closeMobileMenu` twice, corrupting active state and causing double-close on mobile.
findings.tp_fp_justification: Verified in menu.ts: the `navMenuContent.addEventListener('click', ...)` block is placed after the closing brace of the `if (!navMenuContent.dataset.authEventsBound)` guard. If `createLeftSideMenu` is called multiple times, duplicate click listeners accumulate on `navMenuContent`, causing `setActiveMenuItem` and `closeMobileMenu` to fire multiple times per click. The `menuOverlay` and `closeBtn` click listeners have the same unguarded issue.
findings.severity_justification: If `createLeftSideMenu` (or `initMainPage`) is called more than once — which is possible given the dev loader does call `renderMainPage` — duplicate handlers accumulate and corrupt active state tracking and mobile menu behavior. Functional degradation on repeated calls.
findings.category_justification: The missing de-duplication guard causes incorrect behavior (duplicate event handler registration) when the function is called more than once.

findings.message: `menuToggle.addEventListener`, `collapseBtn.addEventListener`, `menuOverlay.addEventListener`, `closeBtn.addEventListener`, and `navMenu.addEventListener` are each added unconditionally on every `createLeftSideMenu` call. There is no guard preventing duplicate registrations. If `createLeftSideMenu` is called twice, toggle/collapse/overlay click events fire twice — e.g., a single toggle click would open and immediately close the menu.
findings.tp_fp_justification: Verified in menu.ts: `navMenu.addEventListener`, `menuToggle.addEventListener`, `collapseBtn.addEventListener`, `menuOverlay.addEventListener`, and `closeBtn.addEventListener` are all added unconditionally inside `createLeftSideMenu` with no de-duplication guard. Unlike the auth event listeners which are guarded by `authEventsBound`, these have no equivalent protection. Multiple calls to `createLeftSideMenu` would register duplicate handlers causing double-fire behavior.
findings.severity_justification: If `createLeftSideMenu` is called more than once, toggle clicks would trigger both open and close in the same event cycle, breaking mobile menu interaction entirely. This is a real functional regression on repeated initialization.
findings.category_justification: Duplicate event listener registration causes incorrect behavior — actions fire multiple times, leading to contradictory state changes like immediately toggling back after opening.

findings.message: The global `button, [role="button"]` rule forces `border: none`, `padding`, `min-height`, and `min-width` on every button in the application. This overrides component-specific button styles (e.g., `.btn-light` which deliberately has a visible border, `.btn-outline`, and form submit buttons). The forced `min-height` and `min-width` to `var(--min-touch-target)` will also inflate icon-only or inline buttons. This broad reset will cause visual regressions across many UI components.
findings.tp_fp_justification: Verified: the global `button, [role='button']` rule sets `border: none`, `padding`, `min-height`, and `min-width` on all buttons. While class-based rules like `.btn-light` and `.btn-outline` have higher specificity and will override it for explicitly-styled buttons, the many legacy pane buttons without class overrides will have their borders stripped and forced min-dimensions applied. The finding is factually correct about the risk of regressions.
findings.severity_justification: This is a dev-only file so it doesn't affect production directly, but it does affect the dev preview environment used to build and validate the UI. Legacy pane buttons without class overrides will visually regress, making development harder. Medium rather than high given the dev-only scope.
findings.category_justification: Overly broad CSS rules that override component-specific styles and break visual consistency across the codebase fall under maintainability concerns.

findings.message: `.input--checkbox` is defined twice with identical selectors (lines 607–615 and 618–628). Only the second definition (with `accent-color`) takes effect; the first is dead code. This is a copy-paste error; the two rules should be merged into one.
findings.tp_fp_justification: Verified in the file: `.input--checkbox` is defined twice consecutively. The first definition has 6 properties; the second has the same 6 properties plus `accent-color`. Since the second rule comes later with identical specificity, it overrides all shared declarations, making the first definition completely redundant dead code.
findings.severity_justification: No functional impact since the second definition wins and includes all properties of the first. This is purely a code quality/maintainability issue with no runtime consequences.
findings.category_justification: Duplicate CSS rule block is a copy-paste error that creates dead code and should be cleaned up for clarity.

findings.message: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` and `@media (prefers-contrast: high)` blocks appear twice in the same file (once around line 1588 and again around line 1711, noted as '/* copied from profile-pane */'). The second block silently overrides the first. This is dead duplication and makes future maintenance error-prone.
findings.tp_fp_justification: Verified: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` with the `*, *::before, *::after` block appears at lines 1588-1596 and again at lines 1711-1718. `@media (prefers-contrast: high)` with identical `:root` variable overrides appears at lines 1598-1604 and again at lines 1719-1726. The duplicates are explicitly marked '/* copied from profile-pane */' confirming it was a copy-paste addition.
findings.severity_justification: Duplicate media query blocks with identical content have no functional impact since CSS rules at equal specificity with the same selector in the later block simply re-apply the same values. This is purely a maintainability concern — future edits to one copy won't automatically sync to the other.
findings.category_justification: Duplicate CSS blocks created by copy-paste are a maintenance hazard but have no current functional impact.

findings.message: `.btn-light:hover` sets `background: #1f22de` (vivid bright blue), directly contradicting the purpose of a 'light/cancel' button. On hover the button turns electric blue, clashing with both the design intent and the purple primary brand color. The same incorrect color is repeated in `.btn-light:focus-visible`. This is likely a copy-paste error from another button variant.
findings.tp_fp_justification: Verified: `.btn-light` is a white cancel button with slate border. Its `:hover` and `:focus-visible` states both use `background: #1f22de`, a vivid electric blue completely at odds with the 'light' design intent and the purple brand color. This is a hardcoded color value that appears to be a copy-paste error from another button variant.
findings.severity_justification: This is a visual/style bug affecting the hover and focus states of cancel buttons using `.btn-light`. It causes a jarring color change inconsistent with the design system, but has no functional impact on correctness or accessibility (focus state is still visible, just wrong color). The file is also dev-only.
findings.category_justification: A hardcoded wrong color value in a design component is a style/consistency issue in the design system's CSS utility classes.

findings.message: `getDashboardItems()` is defined without a `subject` parameter, but `menu.ts` calls `outliner.getDashboardItems(subject)` passing the current page subject. The function always bases its items on `authn.currentUser()`, ignoring the caller-supplied subject entirely. For a visitor viewing someone else's profile, this returns the viewer's own pods and panes rather than anything related to the viewed profile, which is incorrect behavior.
findings.tp_fp_justification: The `getDashboardItems` function deliberately returns navigation items for the logged-in user ('Your profile', 'Your friends', 'Your dashboard', 'Your preferences'), all explicitly set to `subject: me`. This is a personal navigation sidebar — it's correct that it shows the viewer's own navigation regardless of whose profile they're viewing. The finding incorrectly characterizes this as a bug. The parameter mismatch is a mild code smell but the behavioral claim that this is 'incorrect' is wrong.
findings.severity_justification: Even if treated as a code smell (unused parameter), there is no functional regression — the behavior is intentionally correct for a personal navigation sidebar.
findings.category_justification: The finding makes a claim about incorrect behavior, which is what would need to be assessed.

findings.message:
`initialValues[field.key]` is produced by `readProfileLinkValues` as a newline-joined string of all values for that predicate, but only the first line is shown in the input (`.split('
')[0]`). When the user saves, `saveProfileLinkValues` will receive only that single value and silently drop any additional URLs that existed on the profile (e.g. multiple `foaf:homepage` triples). Either load/save the full list (e.g. a textarea + parse all lines) or, at minimum, warn the user that additional values exist and will be removed.

Also note the precedence bug here: `initialValues[field.key].split('
')[0] || ''` falls back to `''` only when the first line is empty/undefined, but `split('
')[0]` on an empty string returns `''` (already falsy) — the `|| ''` is redundant. More importantly, if `initialValues[field.key]` were ever `undefined`, `.split` would throw before the fallback fires.
findings.tp_fp_justification: Verified: `readProfileLinkValues` joins multiple predicate values with '\n', but line 264 only displays `.split('\n')[0]`, and the save path captures only the single input value. `saveProfileLinkValues` then deletes all existing statements and inserts only the single value — silently dropping any additional URLs. The crash claim about `undefined` is incorrect (the reduce always initializes keys to `''`), but the data loss issue is factually correct and actionable.
findings.severity_justification: Users with multiple values for link predicates (e.g. multiple homepages) will silently lose all but the first when they open and save the edit dialog. This is a real data integrity concern, though it affects an edge case (multiple values for the same predicate).
findings.category_justification: The code incorrectly discards existing data — a logic error where the load/save cycle is not symmetric for multi-valued predicates.

findings.message: The JSDoc above declares a second parameter `ariaLabel`, and both call sites (`getOrCreateContainer('GlobalDashboard', 'Dashboard')` on line 562 and `getOrCreateContainer('OutlineView', 'Resource browser')` on line 566) pass a label string, but the function signature only accepts `id`. As a result the aria-label is hard-coded inside the function (always `'Dashboard'` for the section branch, always `'Resource browser'` for the table branch), and the value passed by callers is silently ignored. Either add the `ariaLabel` parameter and use it when setting the attribute, or remove it from the JSDoc and from the call sites.
findings.tp_fp_justification: Verified: `getOrCreateContainer(id)` only accepts one parameter despite the JSDoc declaring a second `ariaLabel` parameter. Both call sites pass label strings ('Dashboard', 'Resource browser') which are silently ignored. The aria-labels are hard-coded inside the function as literals instead of using the passed values.
findings.severity_justification: The hard-coded aria-labels happen to match what the callers are passing, so there's no actual accessibility regression at present. The issue is misleading API design — the JSDoc and call sites suggest the label is configurable but it isn't.
findings.category_justification: The JSDoc documents a parameter that the function doesn't accept, creating misleading API documentation and dead parameters at the call sites.

findings.message: The generic asset rule also matches `*.svg?raw` imports, so raw SVG imports can be processed as emitted asset URLs instead of raw SVG strings. Since the new header/menu code passes `?raw` imports to `createUiIcon`, this can produce broken data-URI icons in the production bundle unless the asset rule excludes `resourceQuery: /raw/` or the SVG rules are placed under `oneOf`.
findings.tp_fp_justification: The finding correctly identifies that both the `?raw`-specific SVG rule and the generic asset/resource rule can match the same import, but incorrectly claims this would produce 'broken data-URI icons'. `iconHelper.ts` explicitly handles this with a fallback: 'If webpack gave us a data URL instead of raw SVG, decode it first' — it decodes the data URL, processes the SVG, and re-encodes it. The icons work correctly in both cases, making the predicted consequence factually wrong.
findings.severity_justification: Even if the webpack rule conflict is a config imprecision, the `createUiIcon` fallback explicitly handles both outcomes correctly, so there is no actual user-facing impact.
findings.category_justification: The concern is about build configuration correctness and whether assets are processed as expected by the webpack pipeline.

findings.message: The catch-all image asset rule still matches `*.svg?raw`, so dev builds can emit a URL for raw SVG imports instead of returning the SVG markup. The new menu/header icon pipeline expects raw SVG strings, so exclude raw resource queries here or wrap the SVG handling in `oneOf` to avoid broken icons in `npm start`.
findings.tp_fp_justification: Same issue as the production webpack config finding. `webpack.dev.config.mjs` has the same two-rule structure with `?raw` SVG rule + generic asset/resource rule. But `iconHelper.ts` explicitly handles both raw SVG strings and data URLs with a fallback decode path, so the menu/header icons work correctly regardless of which webpack rule wins. The predicted 'broken icons' consequence is factually wrong.
findings.severity_justification: No actual broken icons in practice due to the explicit fallback in `createUiIcon`; the config is imprecise but not impactful.
findings.category_justification: Build configuration correctness concern about asset processing in the dev webpack pipeline.

findings.message: `OutlineView` is now a `<section>`, but the outliner still treats an existing `#OutlineView` as its table host and appends `<tr>` rows to it (`GotoSubject` creates `TR` children). This fixture will no longer match the runtime expectations and can produce invalid DOM; keep the outline host as a table or update the outliner to create/use a table inside the section.
findings.tp_fp_justification: The PR changed the fixture from `<table id='outline'>` to `<section id='OutlineView'>`, but `getOrCreateContainer` in manager.js returns any existing `#OutlineView` element unconditionally (line 585-587), and `GotoSubject` then appends `<TR>` children to it — producing invalid HTML if the element is a `<section>`. The inconsistency is real and the code comments explicitly say 'OutlineView is a table'. This represents a genuine DOM correctness issue if any HTML shell (including mashlib's production shell) is updated to match this new section-based structure.
findings.severity_justification: If a production shell serves `<section id='OutlineView'>`, the outliner will produce invalid DOM (TR children in a section). The test fixture mismatch also signals a design assumption that could break the full app when mashlib is updated.
findings.category_justification: Logic inconsistency — the outliner assumes the host element is a table but returns a section if it finds an existing element with that ID, then appends TR children to it producing invalid HTML.

findings.message: `friend.location` comes from profile RDF data and is interpolated into `innerHTML`, so a malicious friend's profile can inject arbitrary markup/scriptable attributes into the pane. Keep the SVG insertion separate and append the location as a text node instead of building HTML with user-controlled data.
findings.tp_fp_justification: Verified: line 363 sets `locationLine.innerHTML = \`${locationIcon} ${friend.location}\`` where `friend.location` is a raw string from `store.anyValue()` reading vcard locality/country from a friend's profile. No sanitization is applied. The same function correctly uses `textContent` for jobTitle/organization and pronouns, making this an inconsistent and exploitable XSS sink.
findings.severity_justification: Classic stored XSS: user-controlled RDF data interpolated into innerHTML without sanitization. Any user whose social pane displays a malicious friend's location field would have arbitrary JS executed in their browser session.
findings.category_justification: Direct XSS vulnerability — untrusted user-controlled data from RDF store inserted into innerHTML without sanitization.

findings.message: This editability check uses the WebID subject URI (often including `#me`) instead of the profile document URI that was discovered above (`doc.uri`/`profile.uri`). The existing code in this same render path checks `sparqler.editable(doc.uri, kb)`, so using `s.uri` can incorrectly disable friend-list editing even when the profile document is editable; reuse the `editable`/`profile` result instead.
findings.tp_fp_justification: Verified: line 381 calls `sparqler.editable(s.uri, kb)` where `s.uri` is the WebID (potentially `card#me` with fragment). `defaultPane.js:70` explicitly uses `$rdf.Util.uri.docpart(subject.uri)` to strip the fragment before editability checks, confirming that `editable()` requires document URIs. The same socialPane.ts uses `doc.uri`/`profile.uri` (document nodes) at lines 259/279, making line 381 inconsistent and potentially broken for fragment-bearing WebIDs.
findings.severity_justification: Friend-list editing buttons would be incorrectly disabled for profile subjects with `#me`-style WebIDs (the most common Solid pattern), silently preventing users from managing their social connections.
findings.category_justification: Logic error — using subject URI with fragment instead of document URI for editability check, inconsistent with the established pattern in the same file and codebase.

findings.message: The menu SVG is forced to white here, but the mobile toggle button uses a white background (`.menu-toggle` in `src/mainPage/menu.css`), making the hamburger icon effectively invisible. Use a dark/currentColor icon or change the button background so the control has sufficient contrast.
findings.tp_fp_justification: Verified: the menu icon is created with `'#ffffff'` (white) color at line 18, and `.menu-toggle` in menu.css has `background: var(--color-menu-bg, #ffffff)` with `--color-menu-bg: #FFFFFF` defined in dev-light.css. White icon on white background produces an invisible hamburger toggle on mobile.
findings.severity_justification: The mobile menu toggle button is functionally invisible (white icon on white background), making the hamburger menu inaccessible to mobile users who rely on visual cues to navigate.
findings.category_justification: Insufficient color contrast making a key UI control invisible to sighted users on mobile.

findings.message: Profile link values are read from RDF data and assigned directly to `href`. Existing data is not passed through `normalizeUrlList`, so a malicious profile can publish a `javascript:` or other unsafe URL that becomes a clickable link in the pane; validate the scheme before rendering as well as before saving.
findings.tp_fp_justification: Verified: `appendProfileLinks` reads RDF values via `store.statementsMatching()` and assigns them directly to `anchor.setAttribute('href', uri)` without scheme validation. `normalizeUrlList` validates http/https during save only. A malicious profile with a `javascript:` URI in a foaf:homepage predicate produces a clickable XSS link in the rendered pane.
findings.severity_justification: Requires the user to click the malicious link (not automatic execution), but a social pane listing friends' profile links is a plausible click target. The exploit is straightforward and the attack surface is anyone whose profile is viewed.
findings.category_justification: Unsanitized user-controlled RDF data used as an href attribute, enabling javascript: URL-based XSS.

findings.message: `createHeader` accepts a `LiveStore`, but the account menu ignores it and loads the profile through the module-level `solid-logic` store. Consumers that initialize the main page with a different store will get labels/avatars from the wrong RDF store or no data at all; pass the `LiveStore` through to `setUserMenu` instead of using the singleton here.
findings.tp_fp_justification: Verified: `createHeader(store: LiveStore, ...)` accepts a store parameter but never uses it in its body. `setUserMenu()` is a module-level function that uses the `store` singleton imported from `solid-logic`, not any passed parameter. The `store` parameter is dead code in this function. Any consumer passing a non-singleton store would silently get incorrect user profile data.
findings.severity_justification: In the current codebase all callers pass the same singleton store, so there's no immediate user-visible bug. The risk is latent — it would manifest if the codebase ever uses a different store instance, which is a stated design concern (multi-DOM/extension use cases).
findings.category_justification: Misleading API — an accepted parameter that is silently ignored, creating a deceptive contract and a potential for future bugs.

findings.message: After `checkUser()` resolves, this can show the Mutual tab for an authenticated viewer even when the pane was initially rendered with `me === null`. In that case the real mutual section was never built (only the empty placeholder from the `me && !thisIsYou` conditional exists), so users who become authenticated via session restore see an empty/nonfunctional Mutual tab unless the pane is re-rendered or the mutual section is rebuilt.
findings.tp_fp_justification: Verified: when `me === null` at render time, `mutualSection` is created as an empty placeholder (lines 402-405) with a no-op `refreshMutualFriends`. When `checkUser()` later resolves with an authenticated user, `applyViewerMode('authenticated')` unhides the mutual tab but `mutualSection.refreshMutualFriends()` on the placeholder does nothing — users see an empty mutual friends panel.
findings.severity_justification: Users who experience session restore (returning visit with stored credentials) may see a broken/empty Mutual Friends tab. This is a plausible real-world scenario in production where session restore timing can vary.
findings.category_justification: Logic error in async initialization — UI state is updated after checkUser() resolves but the DOM content that should back it was never built.

findings.message: The header friend count is computed once from the pre-load snapshot, but `streamFriends()` later loads the subject document and can discover additional `foaf:knows` entries. The async refresh only updates the list/details, not these header stats, so the displayed friend count can remain stale after the real profile data loads.
findings.tp_fp_justification: Verified: `friendCount` is computed synchronously from `kb.each(s, knows)` and set once in `createHeaderSection`. `refreshSocialHeader` only accepts `HeaderControls` (no `stats`), and the `streamFriends()` async loop only calls `refreshFriendsList()`/`refreshMutualFriends()` — no path updates the header friend count after async loading. The count will stay stale if the initial snapshot had fewer entries than the fully-loaded profile.
findings.severity_justification: Display-only inconsistency — the friend list itself shows the correct data after streaming, but the count in the header stats badge may remain wrong. Not a data integrity or security issue.
findings.category_justification: UI state divergence — the header stat is computed once from a snapshot and not refreshed when the underlying data is updated asynchronously.
